metadata.title: William Lane Craig vs Austin Dacey — Does God Exist?
metadata.eyebrow: Debate 273 · God at Purdue · Last rendered: 2026-09-28
metadata.byline: Assessments made by 5.6 Sol. — Rubric: Slugfester Reassessment Rubric v2.
metadata.scope: This assessment covers both opening statements, both rounds of rebuttal, and both closing statements (approximately 5:00–1:40:07). The entire audience Q&A, including both speakers’ answers and dependent replies, is excluded. Neither side receives credit or penalty for excluded material; these scores assess the approved formal debate, not the complete event.

theses: A cumulative theistic explanation gains force when independent features of reality are jointly more expected under purposive agency than under unguided alternatives.
Atheism gains comparative support when recurrent features of the world remain less surprising without a perfectly good relational creator than with one.

observations.bio:
Background
    About William Lane Craig
    William Lane Craig is a philosopher, theologian, and founder of Reasonable Faith. His academic and public work concerns arguments for God’s existence, the relationship between God and time, and the historical case for Jesus’ resurrection.
    Biographical source ↗

Background
    About Austin Dacey
    Austin Dacey is a philosopher, writer, and human rights advocate whose work examines freedom of conscience and expression. He is the author of The Future of Blasphemy and created The Impossible Music Sessions, a forum for music affected by censorship.
    Biographical source ↗
